methodology: Title lane-meter rate = whole allocation / (usable stated meters × explicit title lane count). It is not verified construction cost.
Inventory proxy = whole allocation / (stated meters × inventory lanes). Road lane counts are measure-weighted when counts vary along fully covered ranges.

Existing-asset dimensions are recovered separately from funded project length: bridge inventory span/width/lanes, or the union of road section intervals with measure-weighted lanes/widths. Gaps and conflicting or unknown measurements are withheld. Section size never fills a missing funded segment.
Only exact printed section/bridge IDs or a complete exact road name with compatible region/DEO and unique section qualify; no fuzzy names.
Kilometer post brackets map global K station values to section-local measure by interpolation, never extrapolation. Ambiguous or conflicting references are withheld.
Widening needs funded additional lanes; approaches, slope/drainage and mixed scopes are withheld. Bridge span mismatch above 10% prevents the proxy.

Separate existing-bridge asset estimate = allocation / (inventory bridge span × inventory lanes), only for rehabilitation/major repair or retrofitting/strengthening. This is allocation intensity over the existing asset, not a funded-length rate; it never fills stated length or enters high-rate flags. Replacement, new construction and widening are excluded.
Inventory copyright is preserved. Old inventory does not establish the lane count at the FY2027 funded segment.
Inventory proxies remain separate from title-stated rates, historical comparisons and per-meter high-rate flags. No missing funded lane quantity is invented.

assetContext.method: Condition flag: rehabilitation/reconstruction/major repair only, full matched road range assessed Good/Fair with a known pre-budget assessment year. Recent-surfacing flag: rehabilitation, preventive maintenance or other explicitly described pavement work where the full matched range has a positive recorded last-surfacing year within five budget years; unknown/zero values are not filled. Widening, approaches, slope/drainage and off-carriageway scopes excluded. Bridge condition is displayed, but an unknown assessment year prevents the dated flag.
assetContext.limits: Review leads, not proof of waste or incorrect prioritization. Assessment and budget dates differ; later deterioration, structural/safety work or different funded components may justify rehabilitation. Last-surfacing inventory is older and cannot establish that no later work occurred.

coordinateApproximationPolicy: Haversine separation (Earth radius 6,371,008.8 meters) of two printed points, or sum of separately labeled normalized FMR segment chords. Winding alignments can make chord-based rates higher than actual route-based rates. Endpoint roles, funded scope and construction quantities require verification. Coordinate approximations never fill stated lengths or enter high-rate flags. Building-location and mixed-work rates are withheld.
policy: Allocation per stated segment meter is a screening proxy, not construction unit cost. No missing length is estimated from budget, coordinates or another stage.
scope: Domestic DPWH road/bridge selected title/PAP records and 964 Department of Agriculture FMR records. Mixed work separated; flood/MPB/water titles and FAP excluded. Counts are extracted allocation occurrences.

highRateScreen.method: Peers share category, structure group (overpasses/flyovers, viaducts and pedestrian structures separated), official PAP, a data-derived length band, and matched surface/condition/assessment-year context. Unknown context is pooled only with unknown context and remains explicitly unadjusted. At least 20 peers with stated length ≥10m. Candidate rate exceeds both 2× peer median and Q3+1.5×IQR. Chart extremes exceed max(2×median,Q3+3×IQR); sub-10m printed ranges also stay off rate charts. Lane inventory estimates do not enter these per-meter flags.
highRateScreen.limits: Exploratory relative-rate screen, not proof of overpricing. Width, terrain, structures, engineering quantities and funded extent remain unverified. Missing or insufficient peers produce no high-rate conclusion.
